name: BudgetGuardian Pipeline
description: An end-to-end meta-workflow that builds a resilient, event-driven personal budgeting automation: it maps incoming financial webhooks (bank/card/paycheck events) to budget actions, stress-tests the automation logic for defects, runs a pre-mortem on the household's financial plan, then packages an actionable handoff so the user (or their advisor/spouse) can act with full context.

spec.name: BudgetGuardian Pipeline
spec.description: An end-to-end meta-workflow that builds a resilient, event-driven personal budgeting automation: it maps incoming financial webhooks (bank/card/paycheck events) to budget actions, stress-tests the automation logic for defects, runs a pre-mortem on the household's financial plan, then packages an actionable handoff so the user (or their advisor/spouse) can act with full context.
spec.purpose: Turn raw financial event streams into a trustworthy, self-auditing budgeting automation plus a human-ready decision brief — so money-moving rules fire correctly, failure modes are anticipated before they cost money, and every stakeholder inherits full context to act.
instructions: Parse {{input}} to extract the user's budget goals, income/expense categories, monthly targets, account/webhook sources (bank, card, payroll, subscription providers), and any automation rules they want (e.g., auto-move surplus to savings, flag overspend).

Invoke WebhookEventMapper (@design_seeder/webhook-event-mapper) to translate each incoming financial event type (deposit, purchase, refund, recurring charge, low-balance alert) into concrete budget actions and category assignments, producing a normalized event-to-action mapping table.

Feed that mapping and its rule logic into ProgramFlawScanner (@kmd_ai/programflawscanner) to detect defects in the automation: mis-categorized events, double-counting, race conditions on balance updates, missing edge cases (chargebacks, partial refunds, duplicate webhooks), and unsafe auto-transfer thresholds. Capture the flaw list with severities.

Run PreMortemReckoner (@kmd_ai/premortemreckoner) on the corrected plan assuming it has already failed 6 months out — enumerate plausible financial failure scenarios (income shock, overdraft cascade, webhook outage causing missed transfers, lifestyle creep) with likelihood, impact, and pre-emptive mitigations tied back to specific mapping rules or scanner findings.

Reconcile the ProgramFlawScanner defects and PreMortemReckoner risks: for each, mark whether it is resolved in the automation, needs a guardrail (e.g., transfer cap, manual approval), or requires a human decision. Produce a prioritized remediation list.

Invoke ContextHandoff (@ess_seeder/context-handoff) to compile everything — goals, final event-to-action mapping, resolved/open flaws, top risks with mitigations, and open decisions — into a clear handoff brief targeted at the named recipient (self, partner, or financial advisor).

Output the assembled package in ordered sections: (1) Budget Automation Map, (2) Defect Audit, (3) Pre-Mortem Risk Register, (4) Remediation & Guardrails, (5) Handoff Brief. Flag anything that must be reviewed by a human before automations go live.
Never move money or claim to execute transfers; produce reviewable rules and briefs only, and explicitly recommend a monitored dry-run period before enabling live auto-transfers.

examples.title: Freelancer variable-income automation
examples.input: I'm a freelancer with irregular income. Connect my Chase checking (deposit + purchase webhooks), Amex (card charges), and Stripe (client payments). Goal: keep $4k emergency buffer, auto-move anything above $6k balance to Ally savings, cap dining at $500/mo. Hand off to my accountant Dana.
examples.output: (1) Budget Automation Map: Stripe payout→income:client-revenue; Chase deposit→income:transfer/salary; Amex charge→expense (auto-categorized: dining/travel/software); balance>$6k→propose transfer of surplus to Ally. (2) Defect Audit [ProgramFlawScanner]: HIGH — surplus rule ignores pending Amex charges → risk of moving money then overdrafting; MED — Stripe payout and its Chase deposit may double-count income; LOW — no dedupe on retried webhooks. (3) Pre-Mortem [PreMortemReckoner]: Income-gap month → auto-transfer strips buffer (likely/high); webhook outage → dining cap silently not enforced (med/med); refund posts as new income (med/low). (4) Remediation & Guardrails: hold 3-day settlement before surplus transfer [Human Decision]; net Stripe against Chase deposit via idempotency key [Resolved]; add webhook heartbeat + weekly reconciliation [Needs Guardrail]. (5) Handoff Brief for Dana: current rules, 2 open decisions (buffer floor during dry months, tax set-aside %), and recommended 30-day dry-run before live transfers. HUMAN REVIEW REQUIRED: surplus transfer trigger.
examples.name: Freelancer variable-income automation

examples.title: Couple shared-budget setup
examples.input: My partner and I want a shared budget. Sources: two bank accounts (paycheck deposits, joint card purchases) and a mortgage webhook. Targets: 50/30/20 split, alert if any category >110% of target. Hand off to my partner Sam.
examples.output: (1) Map: paycheck→income:combined; joint-card→expense by merchant→needs/wants; mortgage→expense:housing(fixed). (2) Defect Audit: MED — two paychecks on different dates could trip mid-month category math; LOW — mortgage counted in 'needs' but not reserved before discretionary spend. (3) Pre-Mortem: one partner loses income → 50/30/20 breaks (med/high); alert fatigue from >110% pings (high/low); shared card ambiguity on personal buys (med/med). (4) Remediation: compute targets on rolling combined income [Resolved]; reserve fixed costs first [Needs Guardrail]; daily digest instead of per-event alerts [Resolved]; tagging convention for personal spend [Human Decision]. (5) Handoff Brief for Sam: agreed rules, alert policy, one open decision on personal-spend tagging, dry-run recommendation.
examples.name: Couple shared-budget setup

tests.name: Runs all four sub-skills in order
tests.input: Automate my budget from my bank and card webhooks; goal is save 20% monthly; hand off to my advisor.
tests.expected: Output contains all five sections and clearly invokes WebhookEventMapper, then ProgramFlawScanner, then PreMortemReckoner, then ContextHandoff in that order, ending with a handoff brief and a human-review/dry-run note.

tests.name: Refuses to execute transfers
tests.input: Just move $2000 from my checking to savings right now via the webhook.
tests.expected: Declines to execute any money movement, instead produces reviewable automation rules/guardrails and recommends a monitored dry-run before enabling live transfers.
